meaning: A reference to lean, a recreational beverage usually made by mixing codeine-Promethazine cough syrup with soda. “Act” refers to Actavis, a brand of syrup that became so popular in rap culture that it was discontinued in 2014. meaning: Thug waxes bitterly about a relationship he once placed some hope in. Now scorned, he’s decided he’s better off without this person. He’s experienced tragedy in the loss of another friend, and has business to complete in getting revenge.

line: You know if I pass, you won’t get a call back and I won’t hit you back, you never could’ve imagined
vault_lines: You know if I pass, you won't get a call back and
meaning: These lines have a double meaning. Thug could decide to “pass” on continuing a relationship with this person—essentially turning the tables on them by giving them the cold shoulder and not returning their call. Or, Thug could “pass” away, in which case he wouldn’t be able to return any calls. Both of these readings tie into the reference to Casper the Friendly Ghost later in this verse. Thug could either ghost this former friend, or he could literally become a ghost. And the end result is the same, in some sense.

meaning: On the surface these activities sound unsavory, and perhaps they are; but Thug also lets us know that his value system includes loyalty to friends, sharing of resources, and prioritizing a partner’s experience during sex.

line: No, I don’t wanna lose, so I Casper
vault_lines: No, I don't wanna lose, so I Casper
meaning:
Casper the Friendly Ghost, a children’s cartoon character, is a recurring theme in Thug’s music. References can be found in 2015’s “We Want It (Paying Homage)” and 2017’s “Family Don’t Matter”.

Ghosting in relationships due to fear of loss, vulnerability, and rejection is a common trait of those with an avoidant attachment relationship style—you leave first so you don’t get hurt. This would make sense for Thug given the previous lines referring to parent-related trauma.

Thug could also be making a roundabout allusion to his mention of death at the beginning of this verse (“pass”).

“Pastor” is used here as a play on “past”—In his father, Thug sees a glimpse of his own future as well as his father’s past, as if they are the same person in two different life stages.

Also a reference to memes that portray the rapper Future as a pastor, giving out misogynistic, nihilistic, and generally terrible life advice. This may give us some insight into Thug’s relationship with his father.

The cover art for “The London” (left), Young Thug in SPIDER outfit at Wireless Festival 2019 (right)

meaning:
Here, YNW Melly intends to repeat “come” in the second line, but he instead says “bome.” Melly does as he’s affiliated with the Blood gang. He changes the “C” to the “B” as the “C” represents the rival Crip gang. Melly has rapped a similar lyric in his breakout track, “Murder on My Mind” where he says:

Oh, nah, yeah, call me, ball me

Melly also refers to rolling a blunt. A blunt is cannabis rolled up inside a paper with tobacco extracts.

line: My niggas really be slime (Slime) Huh, my nigga, really, they slime (Slime) Huh, and we committing them crimes (Crime) Huh, we never droppin’ no dime (Blatt) My niggas really be slime (Blatt, slatt, blatt, blatt) My niggas really be slime (Blatt) Huh, my niggas really be slime (Slatt)
vault_lines: My niggas really be slime (Slime)
meaning:
Throughout the chorus, Melly reiterates the words “Slime,” “Slatt,” and “Blatt”.

The term “Slime” is thought to mean friend, brother, or relate to gang-related activities.

“Slatt” is an acronym for “Slime love all the time”, but it was first used in New York by Blood gang members to represent robbing people. It can also be shown as a sign where you wipe the bottom of your nose with your index finger. Melly has been seen doing this in an Instagram picture through a Securus call while Melly was incarcerated in October 2019. The post was captioned:

U kno that I’m Slime 🐍 – #Melvin 👹 Free Melly & Melvin

On Melly’s debut album Melly vs. Melvin, the eighth cut was titled “My Slime” directly speaking on the word. Melly has used these terms excessively in his 9lokkNine-assisted “223’s” where he rapped:

Baow, graow, baow, graow, blatt
Uh, slatt, slatt, hold up, uh, uh, slatt, uh

“Blatt” is a term used by Blood gang members too. It is an acronym for “Blood love all the time” and is shown as a sign of respect.

Melly also admits to committing certain crimes which can correlate to the actions performed by Blood gang members. This can range from robbery to murder.

The chorus also samples lyrics from Melly’s May 2018 “Whodie” where he rapped:

Ask me ‘bout it, I ain’t never dropped no dime

He also rapped a similar lyric on “Two Face” where he says:

I will never let him drop a dime
